title: Multiplayer UX Engineering
summary: This reel breaks down the technical and design requirements for building seamless multiplayer experiences. It covers essential patterns like cursor interpolation, deterministic user coloring, and preventative selection locks to ensure smooth collaboration.

transcript.text: Three cursors land on your canvas. None of them are yours.
The server sends 10 positions a second. Your screen draws 60.
Interpolation fills the gaps, so cursors glide instead of teleporting.
Every user gets a color, hashed from their ID.
Same person, same color—every session. Identity you can track from the corner of your eye.
Avatars stack before anyone speaks. Three faces, then a plus five counter.
You feel the room before you read a single name.
Sarah grabs a card. It glows in her color. Locked.
Two people editing one shape is a corrupted shape. The lock prevents the conflict before it exists.
Click an avatar and your viewport follows theirs. Their pans, their zooms—live.
A design review without a screen share.
Multiplayer is a system. Follow for more UX engineering. Save this for your next collab feature.

on_screen_text: Presence: Feel the room before you read a name
Selection locks: One shape, one editor
Follow mode: Click an avatar and follow their viewport
Multiplayer is a system. Presence is engineered, not accidental.
before_after: Raw 10Hz cursor updates (jittery/teleporting) vs. Interpolated 60fps movement (smooth/gliding).
